title: Mr Crabs animation effects (streaming/typewriter text reveal, cursor trail)

config: EffectsConfig with oracle-exact clamps (text duration [1ms,5s], trail duration [1ms,60s], intensity/opacity [0,1], max_tracked_cells >= 1)
Default/From<AnimationDefaults> reproduce exact Mr Crabs defaults: streaming 120ms intensity 1.0; cursor trail enabled, 250ms, opacity 0.35
schedule: TypewriterSchedule with NEVER_MS=-1000 sentinel, MAX_AHEAD_MS=1000, stagger = duration/8
begin_build continues a burst only while now < last + duration and next <= now + max_ahead, else starts a fresh burst at now
next_timestamp hands out monotonically increasing timestamps across rebuilds
tracker: ChangeTracker: dense per-cell render keys (u64 from Cell content/style/flags) and change times (f32 bit patterns of shader-time seconds), sentinel for never-changed cells
row-generation fast path (unchanged rows are not diffed), resize preserves prefix and stamps new cells, max_tracked_cells bounds the store, rgba8 packed texture
reveal: RevealMath with the exact shader formulas: streaming reveal = elapsed/duration, conceal = intensity * (1-reveal) * smoothstep(0,2,dist); typewriter strike = duration/4, future cells fully concealed
RevealPhase Pending/Animating/Revealed; CellReveal carries pos/change_ms/elapsed_ms deterministically
trail: CursorTrail: shape-aware cursor rects (block/bar/underline/hollow), previous/current rect capture on movement, linear fade (1 - elapsed/duration) * opacity, radius = 0.5*max(w,h), segment between centers, focus/visibility/degenerate guards
GradientCache: bounded LRU gradient resource descriptors (MAX_GRADIENTS=16) keyed by quantized radius
coords: CellMetricsUniform port of iCellMetrics: (cell width, signed row step, row-zero origin x/y); bottom-up orientation uses negative row step and flipped origin
cell_coord maps fragments to change-texture rows (row 0 = top grid row) on both orientations
model: EffectsModel::new(config, size, cell), apply_frame(frame, now_ms, focus) -> &EffectsFrame, set_config, needs_frame, change_texture/change_texture_dirty/clear_change_texture_dirty, last_change_ms, retained_capacity
needs_frame matches oracle textAnimationAnimating/cursorTrailAnimating: frames while a reveal or fade is in progress; future typewriter timestamps keep frames scheduled; expiry yields zero frames
disabled path (text none + trail off) retains exactly 0 bytes and schedules nothing
monotonic clock clamp; text integrity (model never mutates frame content)
element: should_request_animation_with(frame, transitioning, effects_active) additive scheduling helper
TerminalElement::with_effects_active builder and paint wiring: animation frames while effects demand, zero frames at expiry
terminal: FrameDelta::empty(size) additive constructor for synthetic corpus frames

acceptance: Every S9 manifest item maps to production code in mr-crabs-effects plus the two additive element/terminal APIs
s9-effects.json contains provenance-cited oracle cases; deterministic frame sequences match fixtures exactly (1e-9 float tolerance)
Zero frames after expiry: needs_frame false once the last change timestamp + duration elapses (streaming and typewriter cases)
Disabled path has zero retained allocations and schedules no frames (expected_retained_capacity = 0 case)
Typewriter future timestamps stay hidden (pending list) and keep animation frames scheduled
All payloads and caches have explicit bounds: max_tracked_cells, MAX_GRADIENTS, texture length asserted in corpus
No change to underlying terminal text: model retains only numeric change state
No GUI launch; lead owns all builds, tests, lint, corpus validation, integration, and evidence
constraints: Read the source Ghostty worktree and the frozen dirty-oracle-v2.patch only; do not modify them
Do not run formatting, builds, tests, lint, benchmarks, or the oracle
Do not weaken or alter existing S0-S5 public APIs; all additions are additive
Do not touch other slice crates (mr-crabs-protocols, mr-crabs-graphics, mr-crabs-history, mr-crabs-input, mr-crabs-pty, mr-crabs-config, mr-crabs-oracle, mr-crabs-bench, mr-crabs-app)
